setup: Kneel on the floor facing a flat bench, placing a mat under your knees if needed for comfort.
Place your elbows shoulder-width apart on the edge of the bench with your palms pressed together in a prayer position.
Sit your hips back toward your heels so your torso is angled forward.
steps: Exhale and gently sink your chest toward the floor between your shoulders.
Bend your elbows deeper to bring your hands back toward the nape of your neck.
Maintain a slight abdominal brace to avoid excessive arching in your lower back.
Hold the stretch at the point of mild tension for the desired duration before releasing.
instructions.breathing: Breathe deeply and rhythmically through your nose, using each exhalation to sink slightly deeper into thoracic extension.
cues: Thumbs to the nape of the neck

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine instead of extending the mid-back.
common_faults.correction: Brace the abdominals and tuck the pelvis slightly to isolate movement to the thoracic spine and shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Elbows flaring excessively wide on the bench.
common_faults.correction: Keep the elbows kept approximately shoulder-width apart to maximize the stretch through the lats and triceps.

precautions: Ease into shoulder flexion gradually if you have an active shoulder impingement or pain.

name: Bench Prayer Stretch
summary: A kneeling mobility stretch performed with elbows elevated on a bench to increase shoulder flexion, thoracic extension, and lat flexibility.
